I am an old man, fifty-eight years, and I have farmed beans here in Tabora all my life without school. This land is not mine, I rent it, so I cannot waste money on fertilizer from the shop — beans also fix their own nitrogen, my fathers taught me this. I will use the seeds I kept from last harvest, mix them with maize as I always do, and the rains will water the plot. My wife and my son will help me weed, and if the weeding is too much when the rains come strong, I will call two neighbors for a few days and pay them with food or a little money.
